subQuestions.questionText: Outline the strategic management process.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete step (1 mark for incomplete/phrase). Max 6 marks. Either Option may be used.

OPTION 1
- Have a clear vision/mission statement/measurable/realistic objective in place. (2)
- Identify opportunities/weaknesses/strengths/threats by conducting environmental scanning/situational analysis. (2)
- Tools available for environmental scanning may include a SWOT analysis/Porter's Five Forces model/PESTLE analysis/industrial analysis tools. (2)
- Formulate alternative strategies to respond to the challenges. (2)
- Develop (an) action plan(s), including the tasks to be done/deadlines to be met/resources to be procured. (2)
- Implement selected strategies by communicating it to all stakeholders/organising business resources/motivating staff. (2)
- Continuously evaluate/monitor/measure strategies in order to take corrective action. (2)
- Any other relevant answer related to the strategic management process.

OR

OPTION 2
- Review/Analyse/Re-examine their vision/mission statement. (2)
- Conduct an environmental analysis using models such as SWOT/PESTLE/Porter's Five Forces. (2)
- Formulate a strategy, such as a defensive/retrenchment strategy. (2)
- Implement a strategy, using a template such as an action plan. (2)
- Control/Evaluate/Monitor the implemented strategy to identify gaps/deviations in implementation. (2)
- Take corrective action to ensure goals/objectives are met. (2)
- Any other relevant answer related to the strategic management process.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss any TWO types of integration strategies.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per strategy heading + 1 mark per relevant discussion point (Submax 3 per strategy). Mark first TWO only. Max 6 marks.

Forward vertical integration (2)
- A business combines with or takes over its distributors down the supply chain/production chain. (1)/The business merges with businesses that were once their customers, while still maintaining control of the initial/primary business activity. (1)
- Involves expansion of business activities to gain control over the direct distribution of the products/services/sells products/services directly to consumers/customers. (1)
- Increases profitability as the intermediary/distributor/middleman is excluded. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to forward vertical integration.
Submax (3)

Backward vertical integration (2)
- The business combines with/merges/takes over its suppliers up the supply chain/production chain. (1)/The business expands its role to fulfil activities/tasks that were formerly/previously completed by suppliers. (1)
- Aims at decreasing the business's dependency on the supplier. (1)
- Enables businesses to cut costs and have influence over the prices/quality/quantity of raw materials. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to backward vertical integration.
Submax (3)

Horizontal integration (2)
- A business takes control of/incorporates/merges with other businesses in the same industry/which produce/sell the same/similar goods/services. (1)/It is the acquisition/takeover of a related business that operates at the same level of supply chain in the industry. (1)
- The aim is to reduce the threat of competition/substitute products/services. (1)
- Increases the market share/sales/profits and enhance production/distribution. (1)
- Suitable for businesses that operate in multiple geographical areas through joint ventures/licencing/franchising. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to horizontal integration.
Submax (3)

NOTE: Mark the first TWO (2) only.
Max (6)

- Conduct medical/psychological tests fairly (1) on employees/when deemed necessary (1)/Use certified psychometric tests to assess applicants/employees (1) to ensure that suitable candidates are appointed. (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the selection procedure as a human resource activity.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete step (1 mark for phrase). Max 6 marks. Either Option may be used. Procedure may be in any order.

OPTION 1
- Determine fair assessment criteria on which selection will be based. (2)
- Applicants must submit the application forms/curriculum vitae and certified copies of personal documents/IDs/proof of qualifications. (2)
- Sort the received documents/CVs according to the assessment/selection criteria. (2)
- Screen/Determine which applications meet the minimum job requirements and separate these from the rest. (2)
- Preliminary interviews are conducted if many suitable applications were received/to identify suitable applicants. (2)
- Reference checks/Vetting process should be made to verify the content of CVs/regarding work experience/criminal records/qualifications. (2)
- Compile a shortlist of potential candidates identified. (2)
- Shortlisted candidates may be subjected to various types of selection tests such as skills tests. (2)
- Invite shortlisted candidates for an interview. (2)
- A written offer is made to the selected candidate. (2)
- Inform unsuccessful applicants about the outcome of their application. (2)/Some adverts indicate the deadline for informing only successful candidates. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.

OR

OPTION 2
- Receive documentation, such as application forms and sort it according to the criteria of the job. (2)
- Evaluate CVs and create a shortlist/Screen the applicants. (2)
- Check information in the CVs and contact references. (2)
- Conduct preliminary sifting interviews to identify applicants who are not suitable for the job, although they meet all requirements. (2)
- Assess/Test candidates who have applied for senior positions/to ensure the best candidate is chosen. (2)
- Conduct interviews with shortlisted candidates. (2)
- Offer employment in writing to the selected candidate(s). (2)
- Any other relevant answer.

NOTE: The procedure may be in any order.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the difference between quality control and quality assurance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete sentence per concept. Max 4 marks (Submax 2 per concept).

QUALITY CONTROL
- System that ensures the desired quality is met by inspecting the final product. (2)
- Checks carried out during and after the production process. (2)
- Ensure that finished products meet the required standards. (2)
- Checking raw materials/employees/machinery/workmanship/products to ensure that high standards are maintained. (2)
- Includes setting targets/measuring performance and taking corrective measures. (2)
Submax (2)

QUALITY ASSURANCE
- Ensure that required standards have been met at every stage of the process. (2)
- Process of ensuring that products are consistently manufactured to high standards. (2)
- Processes put in place to ensure that the quality of products/services/systems adhere to pre-set standards with minimal defects/delays/short-comings. (2)
- Ensuring that every process is aimed to get the product 'right the first time' and prevent mistakes from happening. (2)
- The 'building in' of quality as opposed to 'checking of' quality. (2)
Submax (2)

NOTE:
1. The answer does not have to be in tabular format.
2. The difference does not have to link, but must be clear.
3. Award a maximum of TWO (2) marks if the difference is not clear/Mark either quality control or quality assurance only.
Max (4)

- Investigate problems and suggest solutions to management. (2)

- Make suggestions for improving processes and systems in the workplace. (2)
- Improve the quality of products/services/productivity through regular reviews of quality processes. (2)
- Monitor/Reinforce strategies to improve the smooth running of business operations. (2)
- Increase employees' morale and motivation to boost their spirit in achieving organisational goals. (2)
- Contribute towards the improvement and development of the organisation. (2)
- Reduce costs of redundancy/wasteful efforts in the long-run. (2)
- Increase the demand for products/services of the business. (2)
- Create harmony and high performance in the workplace. (2)
- Build a healthy workplace relationship between the employer and employee. (2)
- Improve employees' loyalty and commitment to the organisational goals. (2)
- Improve employees' communication at all levels of the business. (2)
- Develop a positive attitude/sense of involvement in decision-making processes of the services offered. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Name any TWO types of business sectors.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark per correct sector (mark first 2 only). Max 2 marks.
- Primary (1)
- Secondary (1)
- Tertiary (1)
NOTE: Mark the first TWO (2) only. (2 x 1 = 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the purpose of the Consumer Protection Act (CPA), 2008 (Act 68 of 2008).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete purpose (1 mark for phrase). Max 6 marks.

Purpose of the CPA:
- Promotes fair/accessible and sustainable places for people to sell their products. (2)
- Establishes national standards to protect consumers regardless of economic status. (2)
- Provides guidelines for better consumer information and to prohibit unfair business practices. (2)
- Promotes responsible consumer behaviour. (2)
- Promotes consistent laws relating to consumer transaction and agreement. (2)
- Establishes a National Consumer Commission (NCC). (2)
- Ensures that consumers have access to information they need to make informed choices. (2)
- Promotes the rights and full participation of historically disadvantaged individuals as consumers. (2)
- Ensures that consumers are not misled/deceived by suppliers of goods/services. (2)
- Promotes consumer safety by protecting them from hazardous products/services. (2)
- Strengthens a culture of consumer rights and responsibilities. (2)
- Empowers consumers to take legal action if their rights are not upheld. (2)
- Protects consumers against contracts that include unfair terms which limit the liability of suppliers. (2)
- Protects consumers against unscrupulous businesses such as fly-by-night franchisors. (2)
- Allows for consumers and businesses to resolve disputes fairly/effectively. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the question that follows.

BOTHA ENGINEERING (BE)
The management of Botha Engineering encourages their employees to establish a workplace forum so that they can participate in decision-making. The owners are also aware of their rights as employers.

Identify the Act that is applicable to the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the correct Act.

Labour Relations Act/LRA (2)
(The LRA provides for workplace forums and stipulates the rights of employers and employees.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the rights of employers in terms of the Act identified in QUESTION 4.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete right). Max 6 marks.

Employers have the right to:
- form employer organisations (1) to represent them in labour related matters. (1)
- form bargaining councils (1) for collective bargaining purposes. (1)
- lockout employees (1) who engage in unprotected/illegal strike/labour action. (1)
- dismiss employees (1) who engage in an unprotected strike/misconduct such as intimidation/violence during a strike action. (1)
- not pay/remunerate employees who have participated in a protected strike (1) for services/work they did not do during the strike. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to the rights of employers in terms of the LRA.

NOTE: Accept relevant facts if the Labour Relations Act was incorrectly identified as an answer in QUESTION 4.3.1.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Advise businesses on the role of SETAs in supporting the Skills Development Act (SDA), 1998 (Act 97 of 1998).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete role (1 mark for phrase). Max 4 marks.

Role of SETAs in supporting the SDA:
- Report to the Director General. (2)
- Promote and establish learnerships. (2)
- Collect levies and pay out grants as required. (2)
- Provide accreditation for skills development facilitators. (2)
- Register learnership agreements/learning programmes. (2)
- Approve workplace skills plans and annual training reports. (2)
- Monitor/Evaluate the actual training by service providers. (2)
- Allocate grants to employers, education and training providers. (2)
- Oversee training in different sectors of the South African economy. (2)
- Develop sector skills plans in line with the National Skills Development Strategy. (2)
- Draw up skills development plans for their specific economic sectors. (2)
- Provide training material/programmes for skills development facilitators. (2)
- Pay out grants to companies that are complying with the requirements of the SDA. (2)
- Identify suitable workplaces for practical work experience. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (4)

subQuestions.questionText: State any FOUR aspects that should be included in an induction programme.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark per correct aspect (mark first 4 only). Max 4 marks.

Aspects of an induction programme:
- Safety regulations and rules. (1)
- Overview of the business. (1)
- Information about the business products/services. (1)
- Meeting with senior management who will explain the company's vision/values/job descriptions/daily tasks. (1)
- Tour of the premises. (1)
- Introduction to key people and close colleagues. (1)
- Conditions of employment such as working hours/leave application process/disciplinary procedures. (1)
- Administration details on systems/processes/logistics. (1)
- Discussion of the employment contract and conditions of service. (1)
- Discussion on personnel policies such as making private phone calls/using the internet. (1)
- Discussion on employee benefits. (1)
- Corporate social responsibility programmes. (1)
- Any other relevant answer.

NOTE: Mark the first FOUR (4) only. (4 x 1 = 4)

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the question that follows.

NOKAMA COMMUNICATIONS (NC)
Nokama Communications has a vacant position in marketing. NC uses the intranet, recruitment agencies and social media as sources of recruitment.

Name TWO sources of external recruitment in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark per correct source named in scenario (mark first 2 only). Max 2 marks.
- Recruitment agencies (1)
- Social media (1)

NOTE:
1. Mark the first TWO (2) only.
2. Only award marks for responses that are named in the scenario.
(2 x 1 = 2)
(NB: 'Intranet' is a source of internal recruitment, not external.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the advantages of external recruitment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete advantage). Max 4 marks.

Advantages of external recruitment:
- New candidates bring new talents/ideas/experiences/skills (1) into the business. (1)/Overall efficiency/Increase in productivity may occur (1) as the new worker actively adds value to the business. (1)
- There is a larger pool of candidates (1) from which to choose. (1)
- It may help the business to meet affirmative action (1) and BBBEE targets. (1)
- Minimises unhappiness/conflict amongst current employees (1) who may have applied for the post. (1)
- There is a better chance of getting a suitable candidate with the required skills/qualifications/competencies (1) who does not need much training/development which reduce costs. (1)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the impact of total client/customer satisfaction as a total quality management (TQM) element on large businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete impact). Max 6 marks. Positive and/or negative accepted.

Positives/Advantages
- Large businesses use market research/customer surveys (1) to measure/monitor customer satisfaction/analyse customers' needs. (1)
- Continuously promote (1) a positive company image. (1)
- May achieve a state of total client/customer satisfaction, (1) if businesses follow sound business practices that incorporate all stakeholders. (1)
- Strive to understand and fulfil customer expectations (1) by aligning cross-functional teams across critical processes. (1)
- Ensures that cross-functional teams understand their core competencies (1) and develop/strengthen it. (1)
- May lead to higher customer retention/loyalty (1) and businesses may be able to charge higher prices. (1)
- Large businesses may be able to gain access (1) to the global market. (1)
- May lead to increased (1) competitiveness/profitability. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to positive impact/advantages.

AND/OR

Negatives/Disadvantages
- Employees who seldom come into contact with customers (1) often do not have a clear idea of what will satisfy their needs. (1)
- Monopolistic companies have an increased bargaining power (1) so they do not necessarily have to please customers. (1)
- Not all employees may be involved/committed (1) to total client/customer satisfaction. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to negative impact/disadvantages.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Advise businesses on the impact of total quality management (TQM) if poorly implemented.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete impact (1 mark for phrase). Max 4 marks.

Impact of TQM if poorly implemented:
- Setting unrealistic deadlines that may not be achieved. (2)
- Employees may not be adequately trained resulting in poor quality products. (2)
- Decline in productivity, because of stoppages. (2)
- Businesses may not be able to make necessary changes of products/services to satisfy the needs of customers. (2)
- Businesses' reputation/image may suffer because of poor quality/defective goods. (2)
- Customers will have many alternatives to choose from and the impact could be devastating to businesses. (2)
- Investors might withdraw investment, if there is a decline in profits. (2)
- Decline in sales as more goods are returned by unhappy customers. (2)
- High staff turnover, because of poor skills development. (2)
- Undocumented/Uncontrolled quality control processes/systems could result in errors/deviations from pre-set quality standards. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (4)

questions.title: SECTION C - BUSINESS ENVIRONMENTS (BUSINESS STRATEGIES) Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
Businesses operate in dynamic environments that require diversification and defensive strategies to remain operational in the market. Some businesses apply the PESTLE analysis to identify challenges posed by social and environmental factors. Businesses should be able to evaluate the effectiveness of the chosen strategy.

Write an essay on business strategies in which you include the following aspects:
• Outline the advantages of diversification strategies.
• Discuss THREE types of defensive strategies.
• Explain how the following PESTLE factors pose challenges to businesses:
  o Social
  o Environmental
• Advise businesses on the steps in strategy evaluation.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK BREAKDOWN: Content (32) + Insight (8) = 40

INTRODUCTION (Max 2 marks; any 2 x 1)
- Diversification strategies enable businesses to introduce a wide range of marketable product lines to accommodate the needs of various customers. (1)
- Defensive strategies allow businesses to reduce unnecessary expenses while planning turn-around strategies. (1)
- The correct identification of the challenges posed by social and environmental factors will enable businesses to plan ahead and deal with these PESTLE factors. (1)
- Strategy evaluation enable businesses to identify gaps in the chosen strategy with the aim of developing new/additional strategies. (1)
- Any other relevant introduction.

5.2 ADVANTAGES OF DIVERSIFICATION STRATEGIES (Max 10)
2 marks per complete sentence:
- Increases sales/revenue/income and business growth. (2)
- Improves the business brand/image/brand awareness of the business. (2)
- Reduces the risk of relying only on one product for sales/revenue/income. (2)
- Businesses gain more technological capabilities through product modification. (2)
- Sustained profitability from different product lines during times of fluctuating economic activity. (2)
- Businesses produce more output using less inputs as one factory may be used to manufacture more products. (2)
- Enables businesses to retain their competitive advantage by meeting the needs of current/new customers/expanding into new unexplored markets. (2)
- Allows businesses to remain relevant/functional/operational in a dynamic business environment. (2)
- Enables businesses to establish additional markets in unrelated markets/industries. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (10)

5.3 TYPES OF DEFENSIVE STRATEGIES (Max 12; 4 marks per type: 2 for heading + 2 for discussion; Submax 4 each)

5.3.1 Divestiture (2)
- Disposing/Selling some assets/divisions (1) that are no longer profitable/productive. (1)
- Selling off divisions/product lines (1) with slow growth potential. (1)
- Decreasing the number of shareholders (1) by selling ownership. (1)
- Paying off debts (1) by selling unproductive assets. (1)
- Withdrawing/Divesting their investment share (1) in another business. (1)
Submax (4)

5.3.2 Retrenchment (2)
- Terminating the employment contracts of employees (1) for operational/structural/restructuring reasons/reduce costs. (1)
- Decreasing the number of product lines/Closing certain departments (1) may result in some workers becoming redundant. (1)
- Businesses can reduce prices/offer discounts/incentives for customers/consumers (1) to avoid closing down. (1)
Submax (4)

5.3.3 Liquidation (2)
- Selling all assets (1) to pay creditors due to a lack of capital/inability to repay creditors/bankruptcy. (1)
- Selling the entire business (1) in order to pay shareholders a fair price for their shares. (1)
- Allowing creditors to apply for forced liquidation (1) in order to have their claims settled. (1)
- Companies in financial distress/difficulty (1) may apply for business rescue to avoid liquidation. (1)
Submax (4)

NOTE: Mark the first THREE (3) only. Max (12)

5.4 PESTLE FACTORS POSING CHALLENGES (Max 12; Submax 6 each)

5.4.1 Social (Submax 6)
1 mark fact + 1 mark explanation:
- Customers may not be able to afford products (1) due to low income levels/high unemployment rate. (1)
- Businesses may not be conversant (1) with the local language of their customers. (1)
- Some businesses may lose sales, as customers may prefer to spend their money on medical bills (1) for the treatment of chronic illnesses. (1)
- High crime rate may affect the trading hours of businesses (1) resulting in decreased profit. (1)
- Any other relevant answer.
Submax (6)

5.4.2 Environmental (Submax 6)
1 mark fact + 1 mark explanation:
- Chemicals/Ingredients in business' products (1) may be harmful to customers/result in bad publicity. (1)
- Measures to dispose of business waste (1) may be expensive. (1)
- Packaging of some products (1) may not be environmentally friendly/recyclable. (1)
- Businesses may not be aware that their current practises (1) are environmentally unsustainable/contributes towards an environmental degradation. (1)
- Any other relevant answer.
Submax (6)

Max (12)

5.5 STEPS IN STRATEGY EVALUATION (Max 12)
2 marks per complete step:
- Examine the underlying basis of a business strategy. (2)
- Look forward and backwards into the implementation process. (2)
- Compare the expected performance with the actual performance. (2)
- Determine the reasons for deviations and analyse these reasons. (2)
- Take corrective action so that deviations may be corrected. (2)
- Set specific dates for control and follow up. (2)
- Draw up a table of the advantages and disadvantages of a strategy. (2)
- Decide on the desired outcome that will result in the achievement of business goals/envisaged when strategies are implemented. (2)
- Consider the impact of the strategic implementation in the internal/external environments of the business. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
NOTE: The steps may be in any order. Max (12)

CONCLUSION (Max 2; any 1 x 2)
- Diversification strategies helps businesses to gain a deeper understanding of the needs of their customers. (2)
- Defensive strategies enable businesses to continuously change their work methods aimed at maximising work performance. (2)
- Businesses should be able to deal with challenges posed by the social and environmental factors to avoid decline in sales/profitability. (2)
- Strategy evaluation allows businesses to improve on the quality of services offered to customers resulting in a larger market share. (2)
- Any other relevant conclusion.

ESSAY BREAKDOWN OF MARKS:
- Introduction: 2
- Advantages of diversification strategies: 10
- Types of defensive strategies: 12
- PESTLE factors (Social + Environmental): 12
- Steps in strategy evaluation: 12
- Conclusion: 2
- Content max: 32

INSIGHT (8 marks):
- Layout (L): 2 (intro, paragraphs, conclusion present)
- Analysis/Interpretation (A): 2 (1 mark all headings addressed; 1 mark interpretation 16-32 marks)
- Synthesis (S): 2 (relevant facts/decisions based on question)
- Originality (O): 2 (1-2 examples not older than 2 years based on recent info/trends/developments)

LASO: Allocate 2 if all met, 1 if some met, 0 if none met.

TOTAL: 32 (Content) + 8 (Insight) = 40

questions.title: SECTION C - BUSINESS OPERATIONS (QUALITY OF PERFORMANCE) Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
The financial function plays an important role in the smooth operation of business activities. The correct implementation of quality processes enables businesses to enjoy the benefits of a good quality management system. Large businesses know the importance of implementing the total quality management (TQM) elements in order to reduce the cost of quality.

Write an essay on quality of performance in which you include the following aspects:
• Outline the quality indicators of the financial function.
• Explain the benefits of a good quality management system.
• Discuss the impact of the following TQM elements on large businesses:
  o Continuous skills development/Education and training
  o Monitoring and evaluation of quality processes
• Suggest ways in which total quality management (TQM) can reduce the cost of quality.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK BREAKDOWN: Content (32) + Insight (8) = 40

INTRODUCTION (Max 2 marks; any 2 x 1)
- A sound knowledge of the quality indicators of the financial function may enable businesses to cut down on unnecessary cost. (1)
- A good quality management system could allow businesses to review their quality processes aimed at producing products of high quality standard. (1)
- The commitment of business to improve employees' skills may contribute to the manufacturing of quality products. (1)
- Monitoring and evaluation of quality processes assist businesses to identify gaps in their processes and systems to avoid project failure. (1)
- The effective implementation of TQM elements may give businesses a competitive advantage resulting in reduced cost of quality. (1)
- Any other relevant introduction.

6.2 QUALITY INDICATORS OF THE FINANCIAL FUNCTION (Max 12)
2 marks per complete indicator:
- Obtain capital from the most suitable/available/reliable sources. (2)
- Negotiate better interest rates in order to keep financial cost down. (2)
- Draw up budgets to ensure sufficient application of monetary resources. (2)
- Keep financial records up to date to ensure timely/accurate tax payments. (2)
- Analyse strategies to increase profitability. (2)
- Invest surplus funds to create sources of passive income. (2)
- Implement financial control measures/systems to prevent fraud. (2)
- Implement credit granting/debt collecting policies to monitor cash flow. (2)
- Draw up accurate financial statements timeously/regularly. (2)
- Accurately analyse and interpret financial information. (2)
- Invest in strategies that will assist the business to remain profitable. (2)
- Avoid over/under-capitalisation so that financial resources will be utilised effectively. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (12)

6.3 BENEFITS OF A GOOD QUALITY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (Max 12)
1 mark fact + 1 mark explanation per benefit:
- Effective customer services are rendered, (1) resulting in increased customer satisfaction. (1)
- Time and resources (1) are used efficiently. (1)
- Productivity increases (1) through proper time management/using high quality resources. (1)
- Products/Services are constantly improved (1) resulting in increased levels of customer satisfaction. (1)
- Vision/Mission/Business goals (1) may be achieved. (1)
- A business has a competitive advantage (1) over its competitors. (1)
- Regular training will continuously improve (1) the quality of employees' skills/knowledge/competencies. (1)
- Employers and employees will have a healthy working relationship (1) resulting in happy/productive workers/improved employee morale/productivity. (1)
- Increased market share/More customers (1) improves profitability/financial sustainability. (1)
- Improves business image (1) as there are less defects/returns. (1)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (12)

6.4 IMPACT OF TQM ELEMENTS ON LARGE BUSINESSES (Max 12; Submax 6 each)

6.4.1 Continuous skills development/Education and training (Submax 6)
Positives/Advantages
- Large businesses have a human resources department (1) dedicated to skills training and development. (1)
- Human resources experts ensure that training programmes are relevant (1) to increase customer satisfaction. (1)
- Ability to afford (1) specialised/skilled employees. (1)
- Large businesses conduct skills audits to establish the competency/education levels of staff (1) which may positively affect the quality of products. (1)
- May be able to hire qualified trainers (1) to train employees on a regular basis. (1)
AND/OR
Negatives/Disadvantages
- Poor communication systems in large businesses (1) may prevent effective training from taking place. (1)
- Trained employees may leave for better jobs (1) after they gained more skills. (1)
- De-motivates employees, (1) if they do not receive recognition for training. (1)
- Employees who specialise in narrowly defined jobs (1) may become frustrated/demotivated. (1)
- Employees may not be aware of the level of competency they should meet (1) in order to achieve their targets. (1)
- It may be difficult to monitor/evaluate (1) the effectiveness of training. (1)
- Any other relevant answer.
Submax (6)

6.4.2 Monitoring and evaluation of quality processes (Submax 6)
Positives/Advantages
- Prevents product defects (1) and minimises wastage/customer complaints. (1)
- Good quality checks/procedures minimise (1) the replacement/breakdown of equipment/machinery on a regular basis. (1)
- May be equipped to get things done right (1) the first time. (1)
- Improve performance (1) and maintain high quality standards. (1)
- Improve current and future management (1) of quality outputs/outcomes/impact. (1)
- Provide clear indication about quality aspects (1) that are contributing to the achievement of goals/targets. (1)
- Modify interventions that may improve (1) the efficient use of resources. (1)
- Support management to acquire information needed (1) to make informed decision about processes. (1)
- Cost of production is reduced (1) as deviations from set standards can be corrected. (1)
- Strategies are revised (1) in order to improve the quality of the products/services/business image. (1)
- Allows for quality control checks (1) and procedures at key points. (1)
- Key performance indicators are carefully selected (1) to monitor and evaluate the outcome. (1)
- Benchmarking is used to find best practices (1) in order to determine the competitive position of the business. (1)
- Quality circles meet on a regular basis (1) to evaluate the progress in terms of quality. (1)
- Continuous research is conducted on latest developments (1) to ensure that TQM planning is up to date. (1)
AND/OR
Negatives/Disadvantages
- Large businesses are often divided (1) and the departments work in silos. (1)
- It is difficult to get everyone to communicate effectively (1) and often messages are not received correctly. (1)
- It often takes longer to detect problems (1) or respond to weaknesses. (1)
- It is not viable/possible to check quality (1) of all the products. (1)
- Limited active/accurate monitoring and evaluation of quality processes may occur (1) as some managers may view/apply this TQM element as a mere routine/formality. (1)
- Any other relevant answer.
Submax (6)

Max (12)

6.5 WAYS TQM CAN REDUCE THE COST OF QUALITY (Max 10)
2 marks per complete way:
- Introduce quality circles to discuss ways of improving the quality of work/workmanship. (2)
- Schedule activities to eliminate duplication of tasks. (2)
- Share responsibility for quality output amongst management and workers. (2)
- Train employees at all levels, so that everyone understands their roles in quality management. (2)
- Develop work systems that empower employees to find new ways of improving quality. (2)
- Work closely with suppliers to improve the quality of raw materials/inputs. (2)
- Improve communication about quality challenges/deviations, so that everyone can learn from experience. (2)
- Reduce investment on expensive, but ineffective inspection procedures in the production process. (2)
- Implement pro-active maintenance programmes for equipment/machinery to reduce/eliminate breakdowns. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (10)

CONCLUSION (Max 2; any 1 x 2)
- The quality indicators of the financial function must be communicated to all internal stakeholders to enable them to use cost effective methods to produce quality products. (2)
- The implementation of a good quality management system requires businesses to conduct continuous research on new ways of improving quality. (2)
- The continuous skills development may enable employees to work effectively and meet business targets. (2)
- Businesses should set standards for their operations in order to continually monitor and evaluate their quality processes. (2)
- Businesses that always implement TQM elements are less likely to experience voluntary staff turnover and reduced complaints from customers. (2)
- Any other relevant conclusion.

ESSAY BREAKDOWN OF MARKS:
- Introduction: 2
- Quality indicators of the financial function: 12
- Benefits of a good quality management system: 12
- Impact of TQM elements (Skills development + Monitoring and evaluation): 12
- Ways TQM can reduce the cost of quality: 10
- Conclusion: 2
- Content max: 32

INSIGHT (8 marks):
- Layout (L): 2 (intro, paragraphs, conclusion present)
- Analysis/Interpretation (A): 2 (1 mark all headings addressed; 1 mark interpretation 16-32 marks)
- Synthesis (S): 2 (relevant facts/decisions based on question)
- Originality (O): 2 (1-2 examples not older than 2 years based on recent info/trends/developments)

LASO: Allocate 2 if all met, 1 if some met, 0 if none met.

TOTAL: 32 (Content) + 8 (Insight) = 40
